correctness.summary: Finite uniform perturbations preserve properness because each closed ball for one metric is a closed subset of a bounded-radius closed ball for the other compatible proper metric. Ishiki's density and G_delta theorems therefore restrict to proper metrics on strongly zero-dimensional locally compact Polish spaces. Algebraic independence injects unordered pairs into distance values, which forces every distance-preserving map on at least three points to be the inclusion. O'Hara's rational-independence reconstruction theorem then upgrades finite magnitude reconstruction from abstract isometry type to equality of ambient subsets.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The inspected Ishiki preprint gives algebraically independent genericity in the full compatible-metric space, relatively G_delta rigid proper metrics, and abstract finite-subspace reconstruction from magnitude; the inspected O'Hara paper concerns abstract finite metric spaces. Neither states dense G_delta algebraic independence inside proper metrics, ambient hereditary rigidity of all subspaces, or injectivity of magnitude on all finite ambient subsets. Targeted literature and current SCOPE overlap searches did not locate those statements. The main residual risk is the recency of Ishiki's preprint and the short deductive distance from its theorems.

value.summary: The result places algebraic genericity inside the natural proper-metric class and strengthens global rigidity to uniqueness of every isometric placement of every subspace with at least three points. Together with finite magnitude reconstruction, it makes magnitude an injective ambient fingerprint for every nontrivial finite point cloud simultaneously.

limitations: Strong zero-dimensionality is required by the available approximation theorem.
No quantitative stability or conditioning for recovery from a perturbed magnitude function is proved.
Singleton subsets all have magnitude one and cannot be distinguished by this invariant.
The result is a structural synthesis and transfer theorem rather than a new construction of algebraically independent metrics.
The primary metric-genericity source is extremely recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations remain a genuine originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
